notes: All four videos are SAMPLE synthetic screen recordings with local TTS narration. They are not recordings of real people, clients, or work. No live model was used to produce these fixtures. spoken_at_s values are measured from each case's timeline.json after TTS mux. evidence_window_s values are measured from the deterministic animation timeline in build/generate_videos.py. duration_s is measured with ffprobe on the final mp4. Node states use the directive names: unverified | evidence_pending | supported | insufficient_evidence | contradicted. Engineering's my-player folder had no fixture format at handoff time, so this schema was written to match the team brief.

claims.claim: I can write a spreadsheet formula that totals a column.
claims.notes: The narrator clicks cell B7 at 4.00s, types =SUM(B2:B6) from 5.00s to 11.67s, and presses Enter at 12.50s. From 12.50s to the end, the formula bar shows =SUM(B2:B6) and cell B7 shows the result 1,420.00 (200+350+180+420+270).

cases.notes: Clear pass: one claimed skill, shown end to end, with the completed formula and total visible together.

This is not contradicted: the video never shows contrary evidence, it simply never shows the skill.

claims.claim: I can style a preview box with CSS.
claims.notes: Different domain and layout from cases 1–3 (dark CSS playground with a live preview, not a form or spreadsheet). Four properties are typed and applied: background #40ddf2, border-radius 24px, padding 32px, color #0c1018. The last property finishes at 25.17s. From then to the end the editor shows the complete rule and the preview shows a rounded cyan 'SAMPLE box' with all four rules applied (on-screen counter: Applied rules: 4 of 4).
